clue.text: Group of Magyar fighters repulsed in battle

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the letters picked out are read backwards
a group of letters is taken out of the run of the words Magyar fighters

explanation.surface: Hungarian soldiers are beaten back during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of' lifts YARF from magYAR Fighters, and 'repulsed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a fight or skirmish, a synonym for a battle.

clue.text: Fantastic reception

definitions.meaning: in British schools reception is the ... children enter

explanation.definitionFit: First-class means excellent; reception is the first class of an English primary school.

clue.text: A cloud of smoke said to cause dismay

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a and pall, a pall being a dark cloud of smoke

explanation.surface: A billow of smoke is said to alarm people.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify, to cause dismay.

clue.text: Eastern country included in allies plans

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another, as something included in a group sits within it

parts.note: allies are mates
China is a country of the East

explanation.surface: The allied powers have drawn up their strategy with an Asian nation on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or plot, so the verb sense of plans fits.

clue.text: Pop Idol: alarm as one of the Animals makes appearance

indicators.note: pop means burst, so the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: On a TV talent show, panic as a member of the Animals band turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like part of the show name Pop Idol but signals the rearrangement of IDOL ALARM.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Wife of William S is up for some shock treatment

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: William Shakespeare's wife was Anne Hathaway, giving Anne H

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife rises to offer electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' is a mass of hair, so henna is a treatment for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye used on hair, a treatment for a shock of hair.

clue.text: Article probing rise of Tory party? Impossible

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
a do is a party
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article investigates the Tories' revival, but is told it cannot be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' works because this is a down clue: the word for Tory reads upwards, and 'probing' slips the article between that and the party.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an idiom refusing a request as impossible.

clue.text: Very private place discovered climbing over parts of Crete

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: spot means both a place and to discover

indicators.note: Crete broken into parts and reassembled

explanation.surface: A secluded spot found high up overlooking parts of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the place word upwards in this down clue; 'over' just stacks it above the island's letters, which 'parts of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is an idiom for highly confidential, very private.

clue.text: Swiftlet regularly spotted in this location

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A small swift is seen often in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location.

clue.text: Foreign official, namely, appears in different guises before king

parts.note: viz is an abbreviation meaning namely
ie, id est, is another abbreviation for namely
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An overseas official appears in disguise before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that one word, 'namely', supplies two different abbreviations in turn, both Latin-derived.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official in Muslim countries such as the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Mr Fix-it introduces traveller to member of crew …

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative
an airman is a member of an aircrew

explanation.surface: A handyman brings a salesman over to meet one of the flight crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Fix-it is a jocular name for a handyman who mends things, as a repairer does.

clue.text: … who -look out!- is to land in trouble

parts.note: a cop is a policeman, someone on the lookout
who refers back to the previous clue's Mr Fix-it, whose last part is it

explanation.surface: Continuing the handyman's story: watch out, he is about to get into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to 10 across: 'who' stands for Mr Fix-IT, giving IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.

clue.text: Obliged to accommodate everyone as agreed

indicators.note: to accommodate is to make room for, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: obliged means tied, bound by duty
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Bound by duty to put up everybody, as was arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts or stories that tallied matched each other, so tallied means agreed or corresponded.

clue.text: Location of battle in area near border occupied by servicemen

indicators.note: occupied by means taken over from within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth
RN is the Royal Navy, a body of servicemen

explanation.surface: A battle took place in a frontier region held by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' simply sets the area letter beside the border word; the navy then occupies the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem in the Netherlands was the site of a famous 1944 airborne battle.

clue.text: Circuitous mountain route won't lead this way, believe me

definitions.text: Circuitous mountain route won't lead this way
definitions.meaning: a winding path does not go directly upwards

explanation.definitionFit: Straight up means directly upwards, and is also slang for honestly, believe me.

clue.text: Politician free to join protest about defector?

parts.note: liberal can mean free or generous
a demo is a protest march
C is circa, Latin for about
a rat is one who deserts his side

explanation.surface: A politician has liberty to take part in a demonstration over a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is a member of a British political party, so an example of a politician.

clue.text: Writer goes underground, according to reports

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a rabbit burrows underground

explanation.surface: An author is said to go into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: William Burroughs was an American novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Former spouse is no longer the same after tiffs

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
something that changes is no longer the same

explanation.surface: After quarrels an ex-partner is a different person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are quarrels, heated exchanges of words.

clue.text: Group of musicians wasted chorister's grant

indicators.note: a grant that is wasted is squandered and messed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A choirboy's funding has been frittered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges CHORISTERS plus GRANT; the S of the possessive is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A string orchestra is an ensemble of violins, violas, cellos and basses, a group of musicians.

clue.text: Name that's a no-no for musical title

definitions.text: Name that's a no-no for musical title

parts.words: Name that's a no-no for musical title
parts.note: a girl's name that follows two noes in the title of a 1920s musical

explanation.definitionFit: No, No, Nanette is a 1925 musical comedy, so its heroine's name follows the two noes.

clue.text: Value of property that's fair

definitions.meaning: the value of a property beyond what is owed on it

explanation.definitionFit: Equity is both the net value of an asset and fairness or justice.

clue.text: Couple found drug in short supply at university

indicators.note: the word is supplied short, cut by its last letter

parts.note: a joint is a cannabis cigarette
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Someone discovers narcotics are scarce on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' docks the T from JOINT; UP is the British sense of being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join them up or connect them.

clue.text: Horror film about headless man

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: headless means losing the first letter

explanation.surface: A scary film about a man with no head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horror film' reads as one phrase, but 'Horror' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden terror, a sense of horror.

clue.text: Swearing at a coach during early part of game

parts.note: a coach is a bus
during can mean in

indicators.note: the early part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Players hurl insults at their bus early in the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusing someone means cursing or insulting them, synonymous with swearing at them.

clue.text: Drive one mile at speed, being short of time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: being short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to pelt is to go at speed

explanation.surface: Drive a mile fast, running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short of' removes T from PELT, leaving PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: Indistinct object, black, covering sky

indicators.note: in a down clue the covering piece sits on top

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to sky a ball is to hit it high, to lob it

explanation.surface: A vague dark shape blots out the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A blob is a shapeless or indistinct mass.

clue.text: Authorised escape

definitions.meaning: slang for legitimate, lawful or authorised

explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal for legal or authorised; leg it is British slang for running off.

clue.text: Men, we're told, succeed at snooker club

indicators.note: we're told means heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: knights are chessmen
to pot a ball is to succeed at snooker

explanation.surface: Some chaps are reportedly good at snooker in their club.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are 'men', so KNIGHTS; said aloud it sounds like NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub, a sense of club.

clue.text: I can't manage more than one container

parts.note: a basket is a container
a case is another container

explanation.surface: Someone admits they cannot handle more than a single box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than one container' means two of them, one after the other; 'I can't manage' is a speaker describing themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is someone who cannot cope, the voice of one saying they can't manage.

clue.text: Agitation following drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: Getting nervous after having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of panic or agitation.
